summary: 국내에서는 2004년 4월 홍도에서 처음 기록된 길잃은새로, 같은 해 10월 소청도에서도 기록되는 등 지금까지 기록이 10건 미만이다. 흑해 연안에서 중앙아시아를 거쳐 몽골과 중국 서북부에 걸쳐 번식하고, 인도 등 남아시아에서 겨울을 난다. 갈대밭, 물가의 풀숲, 논 같은 낮은 풀숲에서 곤충을 잡아먹는다.

art.subject: Paddyfield Warbler (Acrocephalus agricola), adult (sexes alike) in autumn: upperparts warm sandy-brown with a rufous tinge, brightest on the rump; a prominent whitish supercilium, broadest and most striking behind the eye, bordered above by a diffuse dark brown line along the side of the crown; dark brown eye-stripe; throat white; breast and belly whitish with warm buff flanks; wings and tail plain brown; short bill with dark upper mandible and pale pinkish lower mandible with a clear dark tip; dark eye; pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: clinging to a reed stem with tail slightly cocked, side view
art.scene: reed and sedge marsh edge in Korea during autumn migration in September, reeds still green with buff seed heads; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view clinging to a reed stem with the tail slightly cocked: rounded head, whitish supercilium broadest behind the eye with a narrow dark line above it, short fine bill with a pale lower mandible tipped dark, warm rufous-tinged brown upperparts, rufous rump, white throat, buff flanks, pinkish legs

adult, side view perched on a twig, wings closed: short primary projection with the wingtips reaching only a little past the tail base, long rounded brown tail, warm brown back, prominent whitish supercilium, white throat, pale buff underparts
art.build: A small reed warbler, smaller than a sparrow and much smaller than an Oriental Reed Warbler; compact, with a rounded head and a rather long, rounded tail that it often cocks. Bill short and fine for a reed warbler, shorter than the head. Legs medium, pinkish-brown. Wings short with a short primary projection; at rest the wingtips reach only a short way past the tail base. Tail longish, rounded, plain, often held raised.
avoid: Do not paint a bold black stripe above the supercilium; that is Black-browed Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus bistrigiceps). Here the upper border is diffuse brown.
Do not streak the back (Sedge Warbler).
Do not paint a long, heavy bill or a large body (Oriental Reed Warbler).
Do not omit the dark tip to the pale lower mandible.
